title: MoE affinity and long-context jitter case study
content:
Summary:

This is an investigative note capturing a set of experiments and traces run in Nov–Dec 2024 around persistent p99 jitter for MoE-backed long-context workloads (models: Qwen-70B-MoE, Mistral-30B-MoE, LlamaX-33B hybrid). The problem: steady-state throughput looked fine but tail latency would spike intermittently (10–30% above SLO) under long sequence lengths (8k–16k) and medium-concurrency (8–32 concurrent requests). Hypothesis space focused on: expert hot-spotting combined with kernel scheduling/PCIe DMA jitter, cross-model co-location interference, and gating prefetch misalignment with KV cache eviction.

Quick findings (TL;DR):
- Primary contributor: expert fanout imbalance causing bursts of large GEMM work on a small set of GPUs followed by short-lived PCIe and GPU scheduler pressure (observed as 18–28% p99 jump).
- Secondary contributor: RPC serialization + thread-pool contention when expert sets switch rapidly between requests (microsecond spikes accumulate across pipeline).
- KV cache churn (long-context) exacerbates remote expert fetches; when local cache miss rate > 12% we saw a non-linear tail amplification.
- OS/NUMA thread affinity mattered: colocated agent processes with non-deterministic CPU->GPU affinity increased jitter variance by ~12%.

Experiment setup (replicable):
- Hardware: mixed fleet: 4x A100-80GB + 4x H100-80GB in same rack, NVLink intra-node, Mellanox HDR100. Inter-node expert RPC over 100GbE.
- Runtime: rtf/v2.3.1 (custom gating instrumentation branch), python harness + loadgen.
- Models: Qwen-70B-MoE (32 experts, topk=2 gating), Mistral-30B-MoE (24 experts), LlamaX-33B hybrid (8 experts + dense layers).
- Payload: prompt length 512 + generated tokens up to 8192 (effective seq len ~8704), alternate runs at 16k target.
- Concurrency: 8/16/32; batching disabled except auto-batcher set to 25ms window in some runs.
- Quantization: FP16 baseline; additional runs with 4-bit quant to study kernel packing effects.
- Tracing: per-token timing, GPU timeline (Nsight), perf trace, RPC logs with timestamps, and custom gating histograms (per-request expert distribution).

Representative traces / numbers:
- Baseline (no colocation, affinity pinned): p50=90ms, p95=180ms, p99=240ms (8k seq, concurrency=16).
- Unpinned/colocated case: p50=95ms, p95=210ms, p99=295ms; variance increased and occasional 400–600ms spikes when expert hotsets overlapped across requests.
- When local KV cache miss rate >12%: p99 shifted +22% on average; tail behavior non-linear when miss bursts coincided with peak fanout.
- Observed short PCIe DMA stall windows (~500–1200us) correlated with large tensor transfers triggered after an expert switch (Nsight mark).

Deep observations:
1) Fanout imbalance + GEMM burst behavior
- Gating distribution (topk=2) still produced long-tail expert counts per GPU due to token-skew in prompts (repeated tokens / DSL-like prompts). Some requests routed to 3–5x more experts than average leading to transient GEMM queueing.
- Kernel queuing on the GPU (many small GEMMs vs fewer large GEMMs) changed scheduler packing and increased SM context switch overheads for ~200–800us windows.

2) RPC + thread-pool latency accumulation
- When remote experts required, the RPC path added ~150–300us per remote call; under multi-expert bursts these micro-latencies accumulate across the pipeline into visible p99 spikes. CPU thread pool exhaustion (default 32 workers) was common when many concurrent requests rapidly toggled expert sets.

3) KV cache eviction and prefetch mismatch
- Long-context means large KV caches. Prefetch window currently sizes based on avg token growth; but when gating changes suddenly, prefetch misses trigger remote KV pulls and PCIe transfers. If eviction runs concurrently, we see transfer retries and stalls.

4) OS/NUMA affinity effects
- In ~30% of runs where processes weren't pinned, CPU->GPU affinity drifted: libnccl/NCCL microrestarts and scheduling jitter amplified tail latency. Pinning agent threads and setting explicit NUMA binding lowered p99 variance.

Short playbook mitigations tested (ranked):
- Enforce per-agent CPU->GPU affinity at container start (systemd/cgroup + numactl). Result: ~9–12% reduction in p99 variance.
- Increase gating softmax temperature slightly to flatten expert selection for DSL-like prompts (reduced 95th expert count by ~15%). Tradeoff: small quality delta in a few eval prompts.
- Expert pre-warming: on request start, issue a lightweight prefetch token to likely experts (cheap KV check). Reduced remote fetches by ~6–8% on average; helped on burst patterns.
- Adaptive RPC coalescing: batch small remote expert fetches per destination in 200–350us windows. Reduced RPC CPU overhead but added ~40us median latency — net positive for tails at high fanout.
- Kernel composition: prototype split-kernel for small GEMM fusion (combine many tiny GEMMs into a single fused kernel). Reduced SM scheduling overhead in hot bursts; complexity high.
- Co-location policy change: avoid co-locating high-MoE and high-dense models on same nodes; pinned as temporary mitigation.

Open experiments / next steps:
- Run a controlled ablation with artificial token-skew inputs to force gating extreme cases and measure scaling of p99 vs expert-skew. (TODO: harness + input set ready, assign @Evan).
- Add per-GPU async PCIe transfer counters in runtime (we have hooks but need aggregation); correlate with Nsight traces automatically. (PR draft exists: runtime#2345).
- Test split-kernel prototype under H100 for numerical/throughput differences; early signs good but needs more validation.
- Explore an on-device light-weight expert scheduler that throttles or delays expert work to flatten bursts (similar to leaky-bucket). Complexity: correctness and fairness for long context correctness.

Notes to self / observations:
- Many of these effects only show under long-context because KV working set pushes more remote fetches; dense short-context workloads rarely see the same magnitude of tail.
- Quantization interacted oddly: 4-bit runs had slightly less jitter in one cluster (likely due to different kernel shapes packing), but worse overall throughput — needs more runs.
- For customer-facing guidance: recommend affinity pins and conservative co-location limits for now; long-term: kernel fusion + smarter prefetching.

Unresolved questions:
- Is the dominant tail contributor the GPU-side kernel scheduler or the network RPC amplification? Mixed evidence. Need a run that isolates network by running everything intra-node with emulated remote delays.
- Do changes to gating (softmax temp, topk) materially impact downstream quality for production prompts? Need an eval sweep tied to production prompt set (Product: @Hannah).

Appendix (commands / snippets):
- pin example: numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 ./redwood-agent --gpu-idx 0 
- perf trace hint: sudo perf record -e cycles:u -a -- sleep 10; sudo perf script | filter
- run harness: python experiments/moe_long_context_harness.py --model qwen-moe --seq 8192 --concurrency 16 --trace-output trace_qwen_8192.json

References / related artifacts:
- runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345 (gating histograms + prefetch hooks)
- Jira: RINF-1342 (MoE long-context jitter investigation)
- Slack thread: slack://channel/C03SERVING/thread/1672345 (early traces + screenshots)

- Mateo: prototype async PCIe counters and add to trace aggregator (PR draft).
- Hannah: run eval sweep for softmax temperature gating changes against production prompt set and report quality delta.

Status: draft — sharing with eng-serving-runtime for comments.

End of note.
